DM Mariam’s rules for underwater combat:
If prepared, a player can hold their breath for a number of minutes equal to 1+ their constitution modifier (minimum of 30 seconds). Given that time moves quite slowly in combat, if you have a constitution of 12 or higher you should be fine. Those of you with a constitution of 11 or lower, please do keep track of how much breathing time you have left and surface for more air appropriately. 
When making a melee weapon attack, a creature that doesn't have a swimming speed (either natural or granted by magic) has disadvantage on the attack roll unless the weapon is a dagger, javelin, shortsword, spear, or trident.
A ranged weapon attack automatically misses a target beyond the weapon's normal range. Even against a target within normal range, the attack roll has disadvantage unless the weapon is a crossbow, a net, or a weapon that is thrown like a javelin (including a spear, trident, or dart).
Creatures and objects that are fully immersed in water have resistance to fire damage.
Any spell or affect that deals lightning damage causes a shock to nearby creatures. If you are within 10 feet of the aoe or path a projectile travels for an effect that deals lightning damage, you must make a dexterity saving throw against the caster’s spell save DC (this includes the caster). On a failure you take half the original lightning damage, and on a success you take a quarter. Anyone already affected by the full spell is not affected.

At the beginning of your turn, if you are wearing armor you must make an athletics check (DC 10 for light armor, DC 15 for medium armor, and DC 20 for heavy armor). If you fail you are unable to move this turn, though you may still take other actions as normal. If you fail by 5 or more, you instead sink 15 feet at the start of your turn and cannot move any further. If you have a swim speed you can ignore this check unless you have heavy armor on, in which case you must still pass a DC 10 athletics check. If you are inordinately heavy (believe there’s a hampstead damnation thing that turns you to stone), the DC is increased by 5 if you have armor (or at 10 if you have none)
Please react to this message with what DC you will have to meet (fish for none) to make sure you understand these rules and are declaring what armor you are wearing. Those of you who normally wear armor will have enough time to take it off on the boat ride should you wish to do so.
